What is DNS server ?
questions.answer: A DNS server translates domain names into IP addresses, enabling users to access websites using easy-to-remember names.DNS stands for Domain Name System.It acts like a phonebook for the internet, mapping domain names (e.g., www.example.com) to IP addresses (e.g., 192.0.2.1).There are different types of DNS servers: authoritative, recursive, and caching.For example, when you type a URL in your browser, a DNS query is sent to resolve the domain name into an IP address.DNS servers help improve internet speed and efficiency by caching previously resolved domain names.

questions.question: How OSI LAYERS WORK
questions.answer: The OSI model standardizes network communication into seven layers, facilitating interoperability between diverse systems.Layer 1: Physical - Deals with the physical connection (e.g., cables, switches).Layer 2: Data Link - Manages node-to-node data transfer (e.g., Ethernet, MAC addresses).Layer 3: Network - Handles routing and forwarding (e.g., IP addresses, routers).Layer 4: Transport - Ensures reliable data transfer (e.g., TCP, UDP).Layer 5: Session - Manages sessions between applications (e.g., establishing connections).Layer 6: Presentation - Translates data formats (e.g., encryption, compression).Layer 7: Application - Interfaces with end-user applications (e.g., HTTP, FTP).

questions.question: What is MPLS?
questions.answer: MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) is a high-performance networking technique that directs data from one node to the next based on short path labels.MPLS operates between Layer 2 (Data Link) and Layer 3 (Network) of the OSI model.It uses labels to make data forwarding decisions, improving speed and efficiency.MPLS supports various protocols, including IP, ATM, and Frame Relay.Example: MPLS can prioritize voice traffic over regular data traffic, ensuring better call quality.It enables VPNs (Virtual Private Networks) and traffic engineering, optimizing bandwidth usage.
